methods.notes: Match the documented FlowConnect name or production vendor service, never bare NUS. Confirm the name/GATT table read-only after connecting before sync, configuration or group commands.

identification.notes: Nordic UART is shared with the Ninebot Z and unrelated peripherals and is not a scan matcher. FlowConnect is the documented open-bridge name; production uses the vendor-specific 49550001 service. Confirm those identities read-only after connecting before any command write.

device.name: Flowtoys Connect Props (capsule 2 / vision) via Connect Bridge
device.notes:
Flowtoys LED flow-arts props (capsule 2.0 light engines, podpoi, vision poi/staff/club/wand) do NOT speak BLE themselves. They communicate over a proprietary 2.4 GHz "flowtoys connect" radio protocol that runs on nRF24L01+-compatible radios. A hardware "connect bridge" (USB or pocket bridge; ESP32 + nRF24) translates between the phone and the props. The official companion app is "flowtoys connect" (Android package com.flowtoys.app, Flutter); accounts, playlists and shows sync through the vendor cloud at api.flowtoys.com, but prop control itself is local.
ARCHITECTURE: phone --(BLE or WiFi/OSC)--> bridge --(nRF24 RF)--> prop groups. The app addresses GROUPS, never individual props: each group has a 16-bit radio ID shared by every prop in it. Five "public" groups use fixed IDs 1-5; user-created private groups get other 16-bit IDs (the open bridge firmware supports up to 100). IMPORTANT SOURCE BOUNDARY: the reviewed open-firmware revision has its public-group transmit loop disabled, so only LEARNED groups are emitted there. Do not infer public- group production behavior from that revision. To group props: from off, hold the prop button ~10 s until the LEDs flash/turn white. To let a bridge learn a group, the props must be awake on their sync page/mode (page 2 mode 1 on older firmware; the current app instructs page 5 mode 1) while the bridge is in sync mode.
BRIDGE BLE — TWO GENERATIONS. The published open-source bridge firmware (github.com/benkuper/FlowtoysConnectBridge) and companion app use Nordic UART Service 6e400001-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e. The open firmware declares RX 6E400002 WRITE-WITH-RESPONSE ONLY; the companion app has separately been observed issuing no-response writes, which is behavior rather than an extra GATT property bit. TX 6E400003 notifies. The bridge advertises as "FlowConnect <name>" and the app requests MTU 48. The production app instead targets 49550001-aad5-59bd-934c-023d807e01d5 with characteristics 49550002-..., 49550003-... and 49550005-...; their roles and framing still require a production-bridge capture.
ASCII COMMAND SET (open bridge firmware; the same parser is fed by USB serial at 115200 and BLE NUS writes; messages end at '\n' or 0xFF):
  's'<timeout_s>   start RF group sync (float seconds, 0 = no timeout)
  'S'              stop sync
  'a'              reset sync (forget all learned groups)
  'n'<ssid>,<pass> set WiFi credentials
  'g'<name>,<mode> set bridge name + radio mode (0=WiFi, 1=BLE, 2=both)
  'w'<group>       wake a learned group
  'z'<group>       power off a learned group
  'r'              restart the bridge ESP32
  'p'<g>,<page>,<mode>,<actives>,<hue>,<sat>,<val>,<speed>,<density>,<lfo1..4>
                   set pattern on learned group g. Actives bitmask:
                   bit0 LFO, bit1 hue, bit2 saturation, bit3 brightness,
                   bit4 speed, bit5 density; values are uint8. A solid
                   color is page 2, mode 7, actives 0xFF with HSV values.
Uppercase public-group parser forms are not an emit path in the reviewed open-firmware revision because its public-group transmit loop is disabled.
RF LINK (nRF24L01+): 250 kbps, channel 2, 3-byte addresses {0x01, 0x07, 0xF1}, CRC-16, no auto-ack. Props are synchronized by a fixed 21-BYTE packed SyncPacket broadcast per group at ~30 ms cadence (5 repeats per change, forced resend every 1 s): group_id u16 @0 (byte-swapped on wire), padding/sequence u32 @2, lfo[4] @6-9, hue/sat/val/speed/density @10-14, active flags @15, two reserved bytes @16-17, page @18, mode @19, and a SEPARATE command flags byte @20 (adjust, wakeup, poweroff, force_reload, save, delete, alternate). Any nRF24 node with these parameters can drive props directly without the vendor bridge.
WIFI/OSC ALTERNATE PATH: the bridge joins a configured WLAN (firmware defaults SSID "flowspace"/"flowarts") or falls back to AP "FlowConnect <name>" (WPA2 password "findyourflow") at 192.168.4.1. It advertises mDNS _osc._udp (instance "flowtoysconnect") and listens for OSC 1.x over UDP (open firmware port 9000; the early companion app sends to port 8888 — check both). OSC addresses: /wakeUp (int group, int isPublic), /powerOff (same), /sync (float timeout), /stopSync, /resetSync, /pattern (14 ints: group, isPublic, page, mode, actives, hue, sat, brightness, speed, density, lfo1-4), /wifiSettings (2 strings), /globalConfig (string name, int mode), /play (string), /stop, /pause, /resume, /seek (float), /rgb/brightness (float).
CONFIDENCE: HIGH for the RF packet layout, RF link parameters, NUS UUIDs, ASCII command grammar and OSC addresses — all read directly from the bridge firmware source Flowtoys commissioned and published, cross-checked against the open companion app source. MEDIUM for the production app's 4955000x BLE service (UUIDs extracted from the official APK's compiled Dart library; characteristic roles unknown). Mode metadata (base_modes.json inside the APK) confirms the page/mode model: modes are numbered within pages, each with default hue/saturation/brightness/speed/density in 0.0-1.0.

credentials.notes: WiFi credentials are sent to the bridge as a cleartext ASCII 'n' command over BLE (no link encryption) and stored in ESP32 NVS. The bridge fallback AP itself uses WPA2 with the fixed password "findyourflow" in the published firmware.

factory_reset.effect: Bridge: clearing the ESP32 NVS ("bridge" preferences namespace) forgets WiFi credentials, device name and learned private group IDs; the open firmware has no reset button — reflash or clear NVS. Props: group membership lives in the prop; re-grouping with the ~10 s button hold overwrites it.

steps.action: From off, hold the prop button ~10 s until the LEDs flash/turn white.
steps.expect: Prop joins/creates a group with a fresh radio ID.

methods.description: Use the documented "FlowConnect <name>" advertisement or the production 49550001 service, never bare NUS. After connecting, confirm the already observed FlowConnect name and inspect the GATT table read-only before sync, configuration or group commands. The open command set has no safe identification query; do not use sync as a probe.

steps.action: Power the bridge from any USB source (dim solid red LED).
Manually select the exact FlowConnect bridge; a Ninebot Z or other NUS peripheral is not a FlowConnect bridge.
Connect using the documented FlowConnect name or production 49550001 service, never bare NUS; request MTU 48 and subscribe to notifications without writing.

Read the GATT table without issuing commands. Confirm the observed FlowConnect name and the expected open NUS RX/TX roles, or the production 49550001 service, before sync, configuration or group writes.
steps.expect: The documented FlowConnect identity and expected characteristic layout; if only bare NUS is present, stop and leave identification unresolved.

steps.action: Group the props (button hold ~10 s from off) if not already grouped.
Only after read-only confirmation, send sync ('s10'), wait for the group to be learned, then drive the group with 'p'/'w'/'z' commands.

setup.notes: No BLE pairing or bonding on the bridge. NUS is not identity: select the exact FlowConnect bridge, then inspect its name and GATT table read-only before any command write. Props must be grouped before the app/bridge can address them: from off, hold the prop button ~10 s until the LEDs flash or turn white; each quick-group creates/uses a group radio ID. For the bridge to learn a private group, put the props on their sync page/mode (page 2 mode 1 on older firmware, page 5 mode 1 per the current app) and start sync ('s' command or /sync OSC) on the bridge.

rejoin.notes: No bonding on BLE; any phone can take over the bridge (only one BLE central at a time — drop the other phone's Bluetooth to hand over). WiFi credentials are replaced in place with the 'n' command.

entities.name: Flowtoys prop group
entities.notes: Control is per GROUP, not per prop: each group ID maps to one light entity. Color/effect go through the set_pattern command (page/mode select the effect; hue/sat/brightness set the color); wake/power-off map to the light's on/off.

dfu_mode.notes: USB HID product string contains "bootloader". Reports are 64 bytes; a leading zero report-ID byte is prepended on host writes. Update and data roles are declared in protocol_details.usb_firmware_update.

enter.notes: Capsule uses the vendor's manual bootloader button sequence (not reproduced here). As a documented alternative for Vision/Club, the ADVANCED USB HID AppReset(Bootloader) request (command 0xFF, subject u32le 1) reboots app firmware into its bootloader.

image.format: ZIP .fwimg with exactly meta (JSON object) and data (raw firmware) entries.
image.notes: The published desktop updater validates the two entries and target metadata before streaming data. Pad the data to a multiple of 60 bytes for transport. Do not substitute another hardware revision's image.

dfu.notes: From the published desktop updater's brain/FIRMWARE-FORMAT.md and brain/HID-PROTOCOL.md, not from an update executed by this project.

recovery.notes: The reviewed evidence does not establish the complete interrupted- update recovery contract; do not promise automatic recovery.

app_reset_application.role: Boot the newly written application after a completed transfer.

app_reset_bootloader.advanced_reason: Leaves normal app mode and begins a firmware-update session.
app_reset_bootloader.role: Reboot Vision/Club app firmware into the bootloader before Update.

data.role: Four-byte command word followed by up to 60 firmware bytes; use the device's acknowledged offset as the write cursor.

update.role: Begin update with u32le totalBytesToSend, u32le crc, u16le vid, u16le pid and u16le hw_rev; the reviewed updater sends crc=0.

container.data_format: raw firmware, zero-padded to a multiple of 60 bytes for transmission
container.meta_format: JSON object with usb_vid, usb_pid, fw_rev, hw_rev, fw_date, git_rev and fw_ident

power_off_group.description: Power off a LEARNED group with lowercase "z<groupId>". The reviewed open firmware does not emit public-group commands.

group_id.description: ASCII decimal learned group ID; 0 addresses all learned groups.

reset_sync.description: Forget all learned private groups. Single byte 'a' (0x61).

restart_bridge.description: Restart the bridge ESP32. Single byte 'r' (0x72).

set_bridge_config.description: Set bridge device name and radio mode: ASCII "g<name>,<mode>" with mode 0=WiFi only, 1=BLE only, 2=both. Empty name ("*") resets to default. The bridge reboots ~0.5 s after this command.

name.description: New bridge name (max 10 chars), or "*" to reset.

set_pattern.description: Set the pattern on a LEARNED group with lowercase ASCII "p<group>,<page>,<mode>,<actives>,<hue>,<sat>,<brightness>,<speed>,<density>,<lfo1>,<lfo2>,<lfo3>,<lfo4>". Actives is a bitmask: bit0 LFO, bit1 hue, bit2 saturation, bit3 brightness, bit4 speed, bit5 density. All other fields are uint8 0-255. Solid color: page 2, mode 7, actives 255, hue/sat/brightness from the desired HSV colour. Public-group emission is disabled in this open-firmware revision.

actives.description: Bitmask of which parameter fields are applied (0-63+).

group_id.description: ASCII decimal learned group ID; 0 = all learned groups.

set_wifi_credentials.advanced_reason: Writes WiFi credentials to the bridge and may drop it off the current network; the password travels in cleartext.
set_wifi_credentials.description: Set the WLAN the bridge joins: ASCII "n<ssid>,<password>". Sent cleartext over an unencrypted BLE link.

sync_groups.description: Start RF sync so the bridge learns private group IDs from props currently on their sync page/mode. Payload is ASCII 's' followed by a timeout in seconds (float, 0 = no timeout), e.g. "s10".

timeout_seconds.description: ASCII decimal float; 0 disables the timeout.

wake_group.description: Wake a LEARNED group from sleep with lowercase "w<groupId>". The reviewed open firmware does not emit public-group commands.

group_id.description: ASCII decimal learned group ID; 0 addresses all learned groups.

characteristics.name: RX (command write)
characteristics.notes: Open-firmware GATT declaration: WRITE-WITH-RESPONSE ONLY. The companion app's observed no-response write behavior is retained as behavior evidence, not a second property bit. ASCII commands use decimal comma-separated values. Only learned groups are emitted by the reviewed open-firmware revision; its public-group transmit loop is disabled, so uppercase public-group forms are not declared as working commands here.

characteristics.name: TX (notify)
characteristics.notes: Bridge-to-phone notifications (NUS TX). The open firmware primarily logs to USB serial; the companion app does not depend on notify content for basic control.

services.name: Nordic UART Service (open bridge firmware)
services.notes: Standard NUS on the published open-source bridge firmware. The phone writes ASCII command strings (terminated by '\n' or 0xFF) to RX (6E400002); bridge status/feedback is notified on TX (6E400003). Request MTU 48 as the companion app does. The production app uses the 49550001 service instead — see the second service entry.

characteristics.name: Characteristic 2 (role unknown)
characteristics.notes: Referenced by the production app; presumed command write.

characteristics.name: Characteristic 3 (role unknown)
characteristics.notes: Referenced by the production app; presumed notifications.

characteristics.name: Characteristic 5 (role unknown)
characteristics.notes: Referenced by the production app; purpose unknown.

services.name: Flowtoys Connect service (production app)
services.notes: Vendor-specific service the production "flowtoys connect" app (com.flowtoys.app) connects to. UUIDs recovered from the compiled Dart library of the official APK; characteristic roles and the on-wire encoding are NOT yet established (Flutter AOT hides the command builder). Candidates: 49550002 write, 49550003 notify, 49550005 auxiliary (e.g. show/file transfer) — unverified. The CCC descriptor 0x2902 is referenced. Needs one BLE capture against a production bridge to pin down.
